newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER SHOWS SUPRIORITY IN THE RAIN.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER SHOWS SUPRIORITY IN THE RAIN.

text.p: World championship leader Michael Schumacher of Germany demonstrated his and Ferrari's superiority in wet conditions again on Friday as they topped the times in opening practice for Sunday's French Grand Prix.

The 28-year-old double world champion clocked a best time of one minute 18.339 seconds, 1.4 seconds better than his nearest rival Italian Giancarlo Fisichella's best effort in his Jordan as the track dried out in the closing minutes.

His Ferrari team mate Eddie Irvine of Britain, whose future is under threat from the Italian team's admiration for Finn Mika Salo of Tyrrell, was not given a chance to go out on slicks and wound up down in 20th place out of the 22 runners.

Irvine's contract expires at the end of the year and Ferrari's option to renew it expires at the end of July. Their inactivity -- despite Schumacher's forthright support for Irvine -- has suggested they are considering approaching Salo to succeed the Northern Ireland man next season.
Italian Jarno Trulli, replacing the injured Olivier Panis in the Prost team, was 19th fastest.
Frenchman Panis suffered double fractures to both legs when he crashed during the Canadian Grand Prix two weeks ago.

Tarso Marques, the 21-year-old Brazilian who was called up to replace Trulli at Minardi was 14th fastest while Norberto Fontana of Argentina who replaced broken arm victim Italian Gianni Morbidelli at Sauber, wound up 18th on his debut.
